title: The 10 cities across the UK with the most haunted pubs
excerpt: A study of pubs with the most reported ghost sightings has been compiled just in time for Halloween.
content:
The Ten Bells pub in Spitalfields. The spooky haunted pub made famous by “Jack the Ripper “ stories (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

A victim of Jack The Ripper, a hanged burglar, Roman legionnaires and a long departed local still supping on his pint are just some of the spirits haunting the nation’s pubs, inns and taverns. Brighton has the most haunted places for a pint outside of London, with more ghost reports at its pubs than any other town or city.

The seaside city has 38 recorded ghost reports, more than twice as many as York, which is often called Europe’s most haunted city. Among the spooky goings-on, the cellar of the Black Lion is said to be haunted by Deryck Carver, believed to be Brighton’s first brewer, who was burnt in a tar barrel for his Protestant faith in 1555.

York by contrast has just 16 pub ghost reports with The Golden Fleece on Pavement said to be haunted by a Canadian airman who fell from an upstairs window towards the end of World War 2. London, with 83 pub ghost reports across the capital, tops the list with the landlord of The Ten Bells in Spitalfields claiming in the 1970s the ghost of Annie Chapman, one of Jack the Ripper’s victims, had taken up residence.

The Black Lion pub in Brighton, East Sussex, has been named the UK's second most haunted (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Express)

Edinburgh has 13 ghosts including William Brodie, a respected citizen by day and a burglar by night, who was hanged in 1788 and has a pub named after him. His ghost is said to dash from the Deacon Brodie’s Tavern across the road to Brodie’s Close.

Sheffield has 11 ghosts including that of an old drinker who sits by the stone fireplace still holding his jugs of beer in the Old Queen’s Head, said to be city’s oldest pub.

The most haunted places to enjoy a drink as the nights draw in and Halloween approaches was compiled by family ski holiday specialists Ski Famille. It used the Paranormal Database, a long-running archive of UK sightings, folklore and historical accounts including ghost sightings by landlords and punters alike.

Alex Dyer, the firm’s managing director, said because “Halloween falls at the end of half-term this year, and with the clocks going back today (SUN), it will be dark by teatime all week. A pub with a ghost story is an easy evening out, and most of these towns and cities have ghost walks running in October.”

However “a few of the pubs with the best stories have closed or changed their names, so check before you set off” and he added: “If you’re taking the children, look up the pub’s family times as well.”
